newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CMI sees "slight improvement" in H2 results.
newsitem.headline: CMI sees "slight improvement" in H2 results.

text.p: Consolidated Metallurgical Industries (CMI) said on Wednesday it expected results from operations to improve slightly in the second half of the year after a poor performance in the first six months.

The ferrochrome producer on Wednesday released results for the six months to December 31, 1996 showing a steep fall in diluted earnings to 43 cents a share from 169 cents in the same period in 1995 following a fall in U.S. dollar prices received for its product.

Directors said trading conditions were expected to improve in the next six months, predominantly in the latter quarter, while the extra costs associated with the commissioning of the new furnace at Lydenburg would not be repeated.
"However, the recent strengthening in the rand/U.S. dollar exchange rate, if sustained, would impact negatively on rand revenue expectations," they said.

They said growth in stainless steel production and consumption was expected to resume this year -- supported by worldwide economic growth prospects -- which augured well from stronger ferrochrome markets.
CMI would in April receive $6.625 million from Japan's Mitsui in respect of the third and final tranche of assets sold to them.
